Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve a smaller instance of the same problem. Each recursive call works on a reduced input until it reaches a simple case that can be solved directly, known as the base case. After reaching the base case, the function returns its result, and each previous call completes its own computation using that result. This process continues until the original call obtains the final answer, effectively breaking down complex problems into manageable steps.
